name: Political Economy of Development
description: This course provides a political economy perspective on economic growth and development, drawing both from Indian and international experiences. Structural factors -- such as caste- and gender-based inequalities and predominance of the informal sector – greatly influence the macroeconomic outcomes of developing countries like India. Economic relations between countries have been shaped not by economic factors alone but by a complex interplay of historical legacies and strategic power play. Given such a context, this course attempts to study a select number of issues. They include state and markets, capital accumulation, inequality, agrarian transition, labour markets, social exclusion, industrialization, and macroeconomic policies.
